section_summary.extract_value: This is the Conclusions section of a study examining sociocultural theory applied to mindful eating in college women. The study found that limited appreciation of the body's functional qualities helps explain the negative influence of family members' self-objectifying body talk on mindful eating behavior. The authors suggest their findings may stimulate further development of contextual and interpersonal models of adaptive eating styles.

section_summary.extract_value: This Conclusions section summarizes findings from a single study examining sociocultural theory applied to mindful eating in college women. The study tested a path model (shown in Fig. 1) demonstrating that limited functional body appreciation helps explain the negative relationship between family members' body-focused talk and mindful eating behavior. The research suggests that interpersonal and contextual factors influence eating behaviors through body appreciation mechanisms.
section_summary.evidence_source: Conclusions section text and Fig. 1 caption describing the multiple indirect effect model.

Asset Caption.extract_value: Fig. 1. Multiple indirect effect model of family fat talk predicting mindful eating via body appreciation (β = −0.02) and functional body appreciation (β = −0.06). Note that all beta coefficients reported for this model adjusted for BMI are standardized. ***p < .001, **p < .01, *p < .05.
